Vendored fork of upstream toolbar_m3e 0.1.1. The patched source lives in this repo at packages/toolbar_m3e/lib/src/toolbar_action_m3e.dart. The patch is activated by the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides path: entry — remove that entry and flutter pub get silently reverts to upstream.

Overview & role

toolbar_m3e is a leaf Material 3 Expressive UI widget package. Hexagonal / domain-layer concerns are N/A — it has no data, service, or routing surface. It renders a token-driven toolbar (top app, bottom app, container) and consumes m3e_design tokens plus icon_button_m3e.

This package is one of four vendored forks of EmilyMoonstone/material_3_expressive pinned in this repo (alongside fab_m3e, navigation_rail_m3e, split_button_m3e). Its patch is the smallest of the four — a single build() method on one widget — but it carries one extra quirk: the fork adds a real dependency (icon_button_m3e ^0.2.1) that upstream does not declare. Re-syncs must re-add it.

What this is

A vendored fork of upstream toolbar_m3e 0.1.1. The fork is pulled in transitively via the m3e_collection umbrella package, and activated by a path: dependency_overrides entry in the root pubspec.yaml. The patched file is packages/toolbar_m3e/lib/src/toolbar_action_m3e.dart (the ToolbarIconButtonM3E.build() method). The patch marker in source is // PATCH (vendored fork).

Glossary

  • Fork — a vendored copy of an upstream package, edited in-tree, pinned by a path: override.
  • Override — the dependency_overrides: block in the root pubspec.yaml that forces pub to resolve this package from a local folder instead of pub.dev.
  • Patch marker — an inline comment tag (// Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH) that flags every block of code changed from upstream. Audit with grep -rEn 'FORK|fork patch|PATCH|vendored' packages/toolbar_m3e/lib.
  • Re-sync — the procedure for re-applying this fork's patches onto a newer upstream version (see §9).
  • M3E — Material 3 Expressive, the motion/shape system this widget implements.

Architecture — the fork contract

The fork contract has two halves: WHY the patch exists (the root pubspec.yaml override comment) and HOW it is implemented (the inline // PATCH (vendored fork) marker in lib/src/toolbar_action_m3e.dart).

The fork contract (shared)

Every vendored fork in this repo carries the same contract:

  • The WHY is documented in the root pubspec.yaml dependency_overrides comment block above each path: entry. Read it before editing.
  • The HOW is flagged in source with // Patched (vendored fork), // Fork patch:, or // PATCH. Every changed block has a marker.
  • The audit command is grep -rEn 'FORK|fork patch|PATCH|vendored' packages/<name>/lib — re-run after every edit and before every re-sync.
  • The doc-gap checklist (every fork carries this debt): add a > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner to the README; backfill the CHANGELOG; fix the EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).
  • The test contract: every fork SHOULD ship a test/. navigation_rail_m3e currently has NONE (highest debt); the other three forks do ship one.

Public API reference

The barrel lib/toolbar_m3e.dart exports four files. The fork only changes the body of ToolbarIconButtonM3E.build(); the public signatures are unchanged from upstream.

ToolbarActionM3E

packages/toolbar_m3e/lib/src/toolbar_action_m3e.dart

class ToolbarActionM3E {
  const ToolbarActionM3E({
    required this.icon,
    required this.onPressed,
    this.tooltip,
    this.semanticLabel,
    this.enabled = true,
    this.label, // used in overflow menu
    this.isDestructive = false,
  });

  final IconData icon;
  final VoidCallback onPressed;
  final String? tooltip;
  final String? semanticLabel;
  final bool enabled;

  /// Optional label used in the overflow menu; if null, tooltip or semanticLabel will be used.
  final String? label;

  /// If true, the action is styled as destructive in overflow (e.g. error color).
  final bool isDestructive;
}
  • ToolbarActionM3E L1-11: Plain model. Unchanged from upstream — the fork changes how the icon variant is rendered, not the model.
  • label L18: Used in the overflow menu; falls back to tooltip or semanticLabel.
  • isDestructive L21: Upstream styles this ONLY in the overflow menu. The fork also honors it inline on the icon variant — error color on the glyph.

ToolbarIconButtonM3E (the patch)

packages/toolbar_m3e/lib/src/toolbar_action_m3e.dart

class ToolbarIconButtonM3E extends StatelessWidget {
  const ToolbarIconButtonM3E({
    super.key,
    required this.action,
    this.color,
    this.iconSize,
  });

  final ToolbarActionM3E action;
  final Color? color;
  final double? iconSize;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    // PATCH (vendored fork): render the real M3E icon button — shape-morphs on
    // press — instead of a plain Material IconButton, and honor isDestructive
    // inline (upstream only styles it in the overflow menu).
    final glyphColor = action.isDestructive
        ? Theme.of(context).colorScheme.error
        : color;
    return IconButtonM3E(
      icon: Icon(action.icon, size: iconSize, color: glyphColor),
      onPressed: action.enabled ? action.onPressed : null,
      tooltip: action.tooltip ?? action.label,
      semanticLabel: action.semanticLabel,
    );
  }
}
  • THE PATCH L13-16: Returns IconButtonM3E (real M3E shape morph on press) instead of a plain Material IconButton. Upstream returned IconButton.
  • isDestructive inline L17-19: Applies colorScheme.error to the glyph inline. Upstream only honored isDestructive in the overflow menu.
  • tooltip fallback L21-22: Falls back to action.label so the icon variant and the overflow menu share a tooltip source.

ToolbarM3E + Tokens

ToolbarM3E (in src/toolbar_m3e.dart) is the toolbar container itself — token-driven colors, shapes, density, overflow handling. Unpatched.

ToolbarTokensAdapter (in src/toolbar_tokens_adapter.dart, exported via show) bridges m3e_design tokens into toolbar colors/shapes. Unpatched.

Enums (in src/enums.dart) cover toolbar type/variant. Unpatched.

Usage playbook

example/toolbar_usage.dart

import 'package:m3e_collection/m3e_collection.dart';

ToolbarM3E(
  actions: [
    ToolbarActionM3E(icon: Icons.search, onPressed: _onSearch, tooltip: 'Search'),
    ToolbarActionM3E(
      icon: Icons.delete_outline,
      onPressed: _onDelete,
      tooltip: 'Delete',
      isDestructive: true,
    ),
  ],
)
  • isDestructive L6-9: The fork renders this inline with colorScheme.error on the icon variant; upstream only styles it in the overflow menu.

5b. Wiring — how a host actually gets this fork

pubspec.yaml (root)

# Vendored fork of toolbar_m3e 0.1.1 (pulled in via m3e_collection).
# Patched so inline toolbar actions render IconButtonM3E (real M3E shape
# morph on press) instead of a plain Material IconButton, and honor
# isDestructive inline. Patch: packages/toolbar_m3e/lib/src/
# toolbar_action_m3e.dart ToolbarIconButtonM3E.
dependency_overrides:
  toolbar_m3e:
    path: packages/toolbar_m3e
  • WHY L1-4: Root pubspec.yaml override comment — auditable reason for the fork. Edit whenever the patch changes.
  • HOW L5-7: path: override activates the fork. m3e_collection still re-exports toolbar_m3e by name; the override redirects that name to the local folder.

packages/toolbar_m3e/pubspec.yaml

dependencies:
  flutter:
    sdk: flutter
  m3e_design: ^0.2.0
  # Fork patch: inline toolbar actions render IconButtonM3E (shape morph).
  icon_button_m3e: ^0.2.1
  • Fork adds a real dep L5: Upstream does NOT depend on icon_button_m3e. The fork does, because ToolbarIconButtonM3E.build returns IconButtonM3E. Re-add this line on every re-sync — the patch does not compile without it.

Hosts almost never import package:toolbar_m3e/... directly. The fork is pulled in transitively via m3e_collection (the umbrella that re-exports every M3E widget), and most apps reach it through appbox_kit's Kit* wrappers. The root dependency_overrides path: entry is the only thing that activates the patch — m3e_collection's own version constraint is unchanged.

Gotchas + re-sync procedure

The fork adds icon_button_m3e: ^0.2.1 as a real dependency to packages/toolbar_m3e/pubspec.yaml. Upstream does not declare it. On every re-sync, after copying upstream's pubspec.yaml, you MUST re-add the icon_button_m3e line (with its # Fork patch: comment) — otherwise ToolbarIconButtonM3E.build fails to resolve IconButtonM3E and the package does not compile.

Upstream honors isDestructive only in the overflow menu. The fork also applies colorScheme.error to the inline icon variant. If you "restore" upstream's IconButton you will lose both the shape morph AND the inline destructive styling — the two changes ship together in the same patch.

Re-sync procedure (shared across all four forks)

When bumping upstream (fab_m3e, navigation_rail_m3e, split_button_m3e, or toolbar_m3e):

1. Bump the fork's pubspec.yaml version: and the root pubspec.yaml override comment's stated version. 2. Backfill the fork's CHANGELOG.md with the new version entry (every fork's CHANGELOG is stale — see §11). 3. Diff each patched file against the new upstream release of the same path. 4. Re-apply each // Patched (vendored fork) / // Fork patch: / // PATCH block by hand. Do NOT copy upstream over the fork blindly — the markers are your only map of what to preserve. For this fork, also re-add the icon_button_m3e: ^0.2.1 line to pubspec.yaml (see §5b). 5. Update the root pubspec.yaml override comment if the WHY or the patched-file list changed. 6. Run the fork's flutter test in packages/<name>/, then run the consuming showcase (appbox_kit_showcase) to confirm the patched behaviour still renders.

Override hygiene (shared)

Never remove a dependency_overrides path: entry without first confirming upstream includes the fix. A "clean" flutter pub get silently reverts the fork to the pub.dev release, and the patch — including its bug fix — disappears with no compile error. The root override comment is the only durable record of why the patch exists. (For this fork specifically: reverting also drops the icon_button_m3e dep, so the build fails — a rare case where the silent revert is caught at compile time.)

Doc-gap debt every fork carries: (a) no > Vendored fork of upstream <name> <version> banner in the README; (b) stale CHANGELOG.md; (c) EmilyMonestone → EmilyMoonstone typo in issue_tracker (present in every fork's pubspec.yaml).

Decisions / ADRs

None. The fork contract is documented in the root pubspec.yaml override comment; no separate ADR was written. The added icon_button_m3e dependency is documented inline in the fork's own pubspec.yaml — the only fork of the four whose patch leaks past source into the manifest.
